question.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA,
$$

Evaluate the repeated integral above given that $D$ is a region in the $xz$-plane bounded by the lines $z=0,$ $x=0,$ and the curve $z+{x}^{2}=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}2x[{y}^{2}]_{y=x}^{y=\sqrt{1-z}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x(1-z-{x}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\,2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,)\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to calculate this double integral, we plot $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/8079d8f9796c1f863a515ced0091c1f420318be1c4bfe0eb2da641bddfa426ce.png)

 

Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(\,2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}(\,2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x[-(1-z)^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=1-{x}^{2}}-2{x}^{3}[z]_{z=0}^{z=1-{x}^{2}}\,)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-{x}^{5}+x-2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{5}+x-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}{x}^{6}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
